settingsInstructions.title: Using ADDOM
settingsInstructions.description: A concise guide to current ADDOM behavior, safety defaults, and where to look when you need a refresher.

items.0: `[[canon:execute]]` lets ADDOM use enabled tools under the selected [[canon:permission_mode]] (`[[canon:ask]]`, `[[canon:autonomy]]`, or `[[canon:full_access]]`).
items.1: `[[canon:plan]]` keeps the turn tool-free and focuses on options, questions, and next steps.
items.2: `[[canon:thinking]]` is for brainstorming and tradeoffs without tool execution.
items.3: Choosing `[[canon:implement_plan]]` switches the chat back to `[[canon:execute]]` before sending.

items.0: `[[canon:ask]]` prompts before risky actions, `[[canon:autonomy]]` suppresses routine prompts, and `[[canon:full_access]]` grants host-level tool execution for the turn.
items.1: Even in `[[canon:full_access]]`, destructive command blocklists still apply to clearly dangerous host operations.
items.2: Command requests are checked against your command-safety policy before they can run.
items.3: Background commands appear in `[[canon:background_jobs]]`, where you can inspect or stop them.

items.0: Project memory stores notes, summaries, and auto-logged context locally in SQLite.
items.1: Older auto-logs can be compressed after the threshold you set in Settings.
items.2: Compressed entries are archived, not deleted, and can still be reviewed.
items.3: Memory activity is visible in chat and in the Memory panel.

items.0: Continuity keeps track of goals, decisions, open loops, errors, and file references across turns.
items.1: Its retrieval scope defaults to `thread + project` and can be tuned in Settings.
items.2: Profiles such as `economy`, `balanced`, and `deep` control how much continuity is injected.
items.3: Continuity events appear in the timeline when retrieval, packet building, or compaction runs.
items.4: Drift checks can warn when a new turn appears to conflict with established context.

items.0: Each approved AI file write creates an artifact revision for that file.
items.1: [[canon:artifacts]] support diff review, rollback/apply, and revision metadata.
items.2: Artifact context can include bounded revision history, not only the latest version.

items.0: Projects, threads, and timeline events persist locally in SQLite.
items.1: Switching provider or model keeps the active thread and can offer context bootstrap actions.
items.2: Reset controls support thread-level, project-level, and full-workspace clearing.

items.0: Long-running tasks such as dev servers, watchers, and detached OpenAI responses may run in the background so chat can continue.
items.1: Use `[[canon:background_jobs]]` to inspect output, stop a task, or review background activity.
items.2: Persisted command output is trimmed to keep timelines responsive.

items.0: Open the global `[[canon:command_palette]]` with `Ctrl+Shift+P` to search actions across ADDOM.
items.1: Use `Up` and `Down` to navigate, `Enter` to run, and `Esc` to close.
items.2: Commands are searchable by title and aliases such as `switch project`, `autofix`, or `outline`.
items.3: Disabled commands stay visible with a reason, such as no active thread or no open editor tab.
items.4: Recent commands are shown when search is empty for faster repeat workflows.

items.0: Assistant answers stream into the chat as response chunks instead of waiting for the full turn to finish.
items.1: Chunk size and cadence depend on the provider and model and are not exact tokenizer units.
items.2: ADDOM smooths chunk delivery in the UI to reduce flicker while preserving real-time progress.
items.3: Reasoning text appears only when the provider exposes it; ADDOM does not fabricate hidden chain-of-thought.

items.0: Each model turn is grouped into a collapsed `Turn [[canon:runbook]]` in chat with chronological actions.
items.1: [[canon:runbook]]s include approvals, command steps, file changes, usage updates, and turn state.
items.2: Turns with file writes show a `Files changed` card with per-file +/- counts, previews, and review actions.
items.3: Undo actions include conflict guards such as `Changed since this turn` to avoid unsafe reverts.
items.4: Reasoning text shown in the UI is provider-only; ADDOM never fabricates hidden chain-of-thought.

items.0: `[[canon:moa]]` delegates parallel agent tasks while the orchestrator keeps final authority.
items.1: Agent roles are configured in Settings and can use templates as editable starting points.
items.2: Delegations enforce limits such as task caps, timeouts, token budgets, and output truncation.
items.3: Budget warnings can require an explicit choice before an expensive delegation proceeds.
items.4: Agent file writes are optional, disabled by default, and staged as artifact suggestions rather than direct disk writes.
items.5: Only the orchestrator can finalize staged agent revisions through explicit apply actions.
items.6: [[canon:moa]] lifecycle events are visible in both the [[canon:runbook]] and the [[canon:moa]] panel.
items.7: [[canon:moa]] can consume substantially more tokens than a single-agent turn, so monitor policy and usage metrics.
